EVIDENCE / SOURCES / METHOD

CHECK THE BASIS.
THEN MAKE THE PLAN.

READY/ is independent. Where a product or guide relies on a factual safety claim, quantity or current public instruction, the starting point is authoritative UK guidance—not a preparedness blog, affiliate list or social-media claim.

LAST SOURCE REVIEW / 28 OCTOBER 2026
Official guidance changes. A review date is not a promise that a page will remain current forever. During a live incident, current instructions from the relevant authority, utility, emergency service or professional take priority.

How READY/ uses evidence

01 / SOURCE FIRST

Start with authoritative guidance

Use current UK government, regulator, public-safety, utility-network and recognised specialist guidance where it is relevant to the planning topic.

02 / SEPARATE

Facts are not prompts

A source-backed fact is kept distinct from a READY/ planning prompt. Questions such as “who would do this?” or “where is this kept?” are organisational prompts, not claims that a public body requires one specific answer.

03 / BOUNDARIES

Do not invent certainty

Numbers, timings and eligibility statements are used only where the source supports them. Where circumstances vary, READY/ should say so rather than imply a universal rule.

04 / LIVE ADVICE WINS

Use the current instruction

Prepared material is for advance planning. During an incident, follow the latest instructions for your location and circumstances.

What the source review does not mean

“Source-reviewed” does not mean READY/ is issued, approved or endorsed by the UK Government, emergency services, utilities, the Met Office, the Food Standards Agency or the NCSC. It means the relevant factual material is checked against sources such as these and framed as an independent planning aid.
